title: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience
description: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience is an annual publication of original research conducted by undergraduates from around the county. The journal was launched in 2004 and was the first of its kind in the country. The journal disseminates the results of undergraduate research in the broad fields of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Nanoscape is an educational outreach project of the Northwestern University Nanoscale Science and Engineering Center (NSEC), which is part of the International Institute for Nanotechnology (IIN), both of which are under the direction of Professor Chad A. Mirkin. This work was supported primarily by the Nanoscale Science and Engineering Initiative of the National Science Foundation Under NSF award number EEC–0755375 AND EEC-0647560.

title: Stability Study of Self-Assembled Monolayers on Silicon (111)
creator: Mark Hersam
C. Reagan Kinser
Hua Jin
Brian Honeyman
Michael Bedzyk
description:
Monolayers on H-Si(111) were formed thermally
using decene and 10-bromodecene.
Samples were subjected to 100 percent
humidity in order to induce oxidation for
upwards of three weeks. The ability of
bromine to bind to the Si(111) and inhibit
oxidation through steric hindrance was
intended to be analyzed. Atomic force
microscopy (AFM), x-ray reflectivity (XRR),
and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)
were used to help characterize the monolayers
and to compare the amounts of
oxidation. AFM showed the step formation
that is characteristic of H-Si(111), and oxidation
could also be seen. When XRR was
used to determine the physical characteristics
of the monolayer, including the height,
surface roughness, monolayer and silicon
interface roughness, and chain packing density,
it showed that the decene monolayer
formed, but the 10-bromodecene monolayer
did not. Measurements taken using XPS
showed that the relative amounts of carbon
absorbed to the surface increased over a
period of 19 days, with a thin physisorbed
monolayer forming from adventitious hydrocarbons
present in the air. Lastly, it was
seen that the decene monolayer on Si(111)
inhibited oxidation.
